addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
=== e097b200f
fix(riscv): vec_dot f32/f16 - no _tu merge into uninitialized accumulators

The tail-undisturbed accumulate merged into vector registers that were
never initialized for the first stripe; seed them explicitly so the
reduction is well-defined at every VLEN.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== b0e7fa472
perf(riscv): one vsetvli per four dots instead of four per dot (F9)

The d4 inner loop ping-ponged vtype between e8 and e32 around every
dot; hoist the vsetvli so four dots share one. 1.26x decode,
1.14-1.17x prefill on top of F8.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== c4d132efa
feat(riscv): Q1_0 gemv and gemm on nds.vd4dots.vv (XAndesVDot) (F8)

Q1_D4 kernels on the stock vendor 4-way dot product, gated by
-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT: the gemv issues nds.vd4dots.vv on the packed
sign planes, and the gemm reads each weight vector once per four
activation rows. Repack-layout tests extended for the d4 path.

Per-layer 3.11x for the gemv at K=51; supersedes the F6 plan for the
gemv path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== 9b843b555
build(riscv): allow overriding the -march base letters and Zc extras

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== f3b73d5b9
feat(cpu): andesim ROI markers and matmul node selector (ROI)

Optional andesim marker-mode ROI around MUL_MAT nodes, a pure selector
(roi.h) that picks the measured matmul node with its host unit test
(tests/test-roi-node.cpp), and the wiring of that selector into the
dispatch loop. Off by default; enabled by the ROI env knobs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== 626071f50
fix(log): print inline when the log worker thread cannot start

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== 150613f99
feat(riscv): prefetch the Q1_0 repack weight stream (zicbop) (F5)

prefetch.r on the sign-plane stream at DIST=1 (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST knob),
applied to all four Q1_0 gemv/gemm sites. The helper is always_inline
so ipa-pure-const cannot silently DCE the prefetch at -Os/MinSizeRel.

K=51 in-model fpga_l3: 2.14M -> 1.39M cycles = 1.54x on top of F4,
bit-exact, shape-invariant across all five layer-7 gemv shapes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== e1479f29a
feat(riscv): Q1_0 row-parallel 64x1 repack path for wide VLEN (F4)

Q1_0_64x1 repack for RISC-V wide VLEN: 64 rows interleave into one
block so the gemv runs row-parallel across the vector length, with a
single bit-index authority for the q1_0x64 sign planes shared by the
repack and the kernels, and structured sign-pattern tests for the
layout (tests/test-repack-q1_0.cpp).

K=51 in-model fpga_l3: 4.48M -> 2.14M cycles = 2.09x per layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Codegen gate for the F5 Q1_0 software prefetch (ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp).
#
# Why a codegen gate and not a result test: __builtin_prefetch has no observable
# side effect, so as soon as GCC leaves q1_prefetch_block out of line (partial
# inlining does that at -O2/-O3), ipa-pure-const marks the helper pure and DCE
# deletes every call. The binary then contains zero prefetch.r, results stay
# correct, and every result-level test - including verify.sh - still passes. The
# only way to see it is to count the emitted instructions. This was real: b-pf2
# and b-pf4 kept the gemv prefetch and silently lost the gemm one.
#
# Reuses an existing CMake build's compile line for that one TU (so march,
# -O level and includes are never duplicated here) and recompiles it to
# assembly at each prefetch distance.
#
# Two dimensions are checked, because both can break it independently: the
# prefetch distance, and the optimization level (-Os stops inlining the helper,
# which is exactly when DCE takes the call away).
#
# Usage: ./check-prefetch.sh [build-dir]      env: BUILD, DISTS, OLEVELS
set -e
LLAMA=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
BUILD=${1:-${BUILD:-b-pf1}}
DISTS=${DISTS:-"1 2 4"}
OLEVELS=${OLEVELS:-"O2 O3 Os"}
SRC=$LLAMA/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp
# entry points the per-VLEN static kernels inline into; each should hold 2
# prefetch.r (the vl512 and vl1024 instantiations)
ENTRIES="ggml_gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0 ggml_gemm_q1_0_64x1_q8_0"

CC_DB=$LLAMA/$BUILD/compile_commands.json
[ -f "$CC_DB" ] || { echo "no $CC_DB (configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON)"; exit 1; }

ENTRY=$(python3 - "$CC_DB" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
for d in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
    if d['file'].endswith('arch/riscv/repack.cpp'):
        print(d['directory']); print(d['command']); break
else:
    sys.exit('arch/riscv/repack.cpp not in compile_commands.json')
EOF
)
CC_DIR=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | head -1)
CC_CMD=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | tail -1)

OUT=$LLAMA/$BUILD/prefetch-check
mkdir -p "$OUT"
echo "build $BUILD, source $SRC"

rc=0

# $1 = label, $2 = dist, $3 = -O level to force ("" = keep the build's own)
check_variant() {
    asm=$OUT/repack-$1.s
    cmd=$(printf '%s' "$CC_CMD" | sed -E "s/-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=[0-9]+//g")
    [ -n "$3" ] && cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s/ -O[0-9sgz]+ / -$3 /")
    cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s#-o [^ ]+\.o #-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=$2 -S -o $asm #")
    ( cd "$CC_DIR" && eval "$cmd" )

    line="  $1:"
    for e in $ENTRIES; do
        n=$(awk -v F="$e:" 'BEGIN{c=0} $0==F{i=1;next} i&&/prefetch\./{c++} i&&/\.size/{i=0} END{print c}' "$asm")
        line="$line  $e=$n"
        if [ "$2" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
            line="$line(FAIL)"
            rc=1
        fi
    done
    echo "$line"
}

for d in $DISTS;   do check_variant "DIST=$d" "$d" ""; done
for o in $OLEVELS; do check_variant "-$o"     1    "$o"; done

if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL: an entry point emits no prefetch.r - the optimization is gone there."
    echo "      Expect 2 per entry (vl512 + vl1024). Check always_inline on"
    echo "      q1_prefetch_block and zicbop in -march."
    exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: every entry point prefetches at distances ($DISTS) and levels ($OLEVELS)"

content.content:
# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK      : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON    : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                            gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N   : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
#   -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME     : HVM redirect selector; only on the HVM build
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack toggle   $3 extra defines (DIST / HVM selector, or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | hvm
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv
    # (XAndesVDot). Q1_D4 also flips the sign-plane order in the repack, so it
    # is a whole-binary switch, not a kernel-only one.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DQ1_D4=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the d4 kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DQ1_D4=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm$SUF"      "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # d4 + the measured tensor placed in HVM. Upper bound on what a big/fast
    # local memory can still recover once prefetch and the dot kernel are in.
    d4-hvm)   cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-hvm$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DQ1_D4=1 -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|hvm|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

#   -static                : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK      : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON    : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                            gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N   : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
#   -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME     : HVM redirect selector; only on the HVM build
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack toggle   $3 extra defines (DIST / HVM selector, or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | hvm
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv
    # (XAndesVDot). Q1_D4 also flips the sign-plane order in the repack, so it
    # is a whole-binary switch, not a kernel-only one.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DQ1_D4=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the d4 kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DQ1_D4=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm$SUF"      "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # d4 + the measured tensor placed in HVM. Upper bound on what a big/fast
    # local memory can still recover once prefetch and the dot kernel are in.
    d4-hvm)   cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-hvm$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DQ1_D4=1 -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|hvm|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

content.text:
Answer: two switches, both at build time.

**vd4dots** - needs both flags together:
- ON: `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` (CMake option, puts `_xandesvdot` into -march) **plus** `-DQ1_D4=1` inside `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`/`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` (source gate `#if defined(Q1_D4)`, also flips the sign-plane repack order, so it is a whole-binary switch)
- OFF: omit both (default) -> plain RVV kernels

**prefetch**:
- ON: default. `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` defaults to 1 in the source, and `GGML_RV_ZICBOP` is ON by default (puts `_zicbop` into -march so `__builtin_prefetch` really emits `prefetch.r`)
- OFF: add `-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` to `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`/`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`

The four combinations, as cmake args:

| build | top-level -D | in C/CXX flags |
|---|---|---|
| repack only | `-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON` | `-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` |
| + prefetch | `-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON` | `-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` (or omit) |
| + vd4dots only | `-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | `-DQ1_D4=1 -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` |
| + both | `-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | `-DQ1_D4=1 -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` |

Your `./build.sh` already wraps these as targets `baseline` / `prefetch` / `d4-nopf` / `d4`, with the full Andes toolchain setup.

One thing to check after this restructure: vd4dots is now controlled by two flags that must move together (`GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT` for -march, `Q1_D4` for the source). If you want one single switch, I can make the CMake option also define `Q1_D4` so `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` alone turns it on.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 prefetch reproduce
# runbook (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md): pristine / baseline / prefetch (+ optional hvm).
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   hvm      = repack + weights-in-HVM (older experiment, now superseded)
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh prefetch           # just the shipped kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 (see q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md shape table):
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 kernel A/Bs:
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 shape table:
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                  : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK        : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON      : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                              gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON  : single switch for the d4 kernels - appends _xandesvdot
#                              to -march AND defines Q1_D4 (kernels + sign-plane order)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N     : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack/vdot toggles   $3 extra defines (DIST etc., or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | d4 | d4-nopf | *-nodpref
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv.
    # GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT is the whole switch: -march plus the Q1_D4 source gate
    # (kernels and sign-plane repack order), so no extra define is needed.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the d4 kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|d4-nopf|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the d4 kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DQ1_D4=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm$SUF"      "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # d4 + the measured tensor placed in HVM. Upper bound on what a big/fast
    # local memory can still recover once prefetch and the dot kernel are in.
    d4-hvm)   cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-hvm$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DQ1_D4=1 -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|hvm|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

狀態跟上次結束時一致,還在 `q1_0-rvv-opt` branch。這次 session 做的事:

**你原本 reset 掉一堆 commit,要求重新拆成一個 feature 一個 commit。** 我用 reflog 找回舊的 32 個 commit 歷史,重新整理過三輪(你陸續加需求):

1. 第一輪:8 個 commit,按你原本的功能線分組(F4 repack、F5 prefetch、log fix、ROI、march override、F8 vd4dots、F9 vsetvli、vec_dot fix),但保留了 HVM 相關檔案。
2. 你說「不要 HVM」→ 整個重做,砍掉 HVM 全部程式碼和測試。
3. 你說「不要 kernel-lab 這些」→ 再重做,commit 裡不含 lab 腳本,只留 ggml 核心改動;順便把 fix 類 commit 折進對應 feature、拿掉 roadmap 編號(F4/F5/F8/F9 這種代號)。
4. 你說「乾脆直上 vd4dot,再加 prefetch」→ 重新排序,做成「standard RVV repack → vd4dots optimization → prefetch → ROI」四個 commit,且 vd4dots 和 prefetch 各自可獨立開關。

**目前分支 `q1_0-rvv-opt` 上的 5 個 commit(在 master 12127defd 之上):**

| commit | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `8734bdb7e` | Q1_0 row-parallel 64x1 repack(標準 RVV) |
| `c4fc0fbc2` | vd4dots kernel(Andes `nds.vd4dots.vv`),`-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` 單一開關 |
| `be88be108` | 權重流 prefetch(zicbop),`Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` 開關 |
| `1c233145c` | andesim ROI 標記與 matmul node selector |
| `5d01611f1` | `build.sh` A/B 建置腳本(pristine/baseline/prefetch/d4/d4-nopf),已改 `.gitignore` 白名單 |

**中途做的驗證,不只是改 commit message:**
- 你要「vd4dots 和 prefetch 各自能開關」時,我用 Andes 工具鏈實際編譯,確認拿掉 prefetch 呼叫後 vd4dots commit 的組語裡 prefetch 指令歸零、vd4dots 指令還在(64 個)。

# Optimizing 1-bit LLM Inference for RISC-V Edge Devices

# Author: Pei-Hsiang Hung, Andes Technology

---

## Abstract

1-bit compression has left the lab. You can download the Bonsai 27B model that fits in
3.8 GB and keeps 90% of its FP16 benchmark score. That moves the edge
bottleneck from 'Does the model fit?' to 'Can the silicon execute it?'.

We targeted an **Andes AX46MPV**: a single hart with a 1024-bit vector unit,
32 KB of L1 data cache, no L2 and 2 MB of L3 -- wide vectors on a thin memory
system, which is what an edge core actually looks like. On it, upstream
llama.cpp used **32 of the 128 available byte-lanes** and paid a serial
reduction every 32 columns.

We optimized the kernel at three levels. Data layout: repack the weights so
every lane owns an output row and the serial reductions disappear. Memory:
prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never reused. ISA: hand the
reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, which is Andes V5 vendor instruction whose
operand shape already matches the repacked layout.

What we measure is the 1-bit matmul kernel that dominates decode time. On
Bonsai 27B it runs **11.86x** faster than upstream llama.cpp on the same core,
with bit-identical output.

We measure the cycle with AndeSim's newly developed hybrid mode: a fast functional
model races through the long-running model load, then hands the machine state to
the RTL engine at exactly the matmul we care about.

## Reference
https://makerpro.cc/how-can-bonsai-27b-disrupt-the-boundaries-between-local-llm-and-slm/

< We found upstream llama.cpp using **32 of the 128 byte-lanes** of a 1024-bit
< vector unit, plus a serial reduction per 32 columns. Three changes fixed it:
< transpose 64 weight rows into the lanes so every lane owns an output row and
< the reductions vanish; prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never
< reused; and hand the reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, a stock Andes V5 vendor

< fast-forwards the 9-minute model load, then hands off to the RTL engine, which
< measures one matmul out of 497. Reproducible to the cycle.

< 
< ## Takeaways
< 
< 1. **For 1-bit models the kernel is a data-layout problem.** Transpose into the
<    lanes first; everything else follows from that.

<    the win before it is portable to any RVV core.
< 3. **Per-kernel pre-silicon measurement changes which optimizations you
<    attempt**, because it ranks them correctly when cheaper tools do not.
<

< 
<

< estimates. Quality-retention figures are the model publisher's, not ours.

1	# Bonsai 8B and 27B on andesim hybrid: one kernel stack, 11.23x and 11.86x
2	
3	Engine `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL); 8B measured
4	2026-08-04, 27B measured 2026-08-05..06. The same Q1_0 optimization chain
5	(repack -> prefetch -> vd4dots) carries from 4B to 8B to 27B with the
6	per-element cost almost unchanged:
7	
8	| model | arch   | K=51 node                       | pristine -> final cycles  | speedup |
9	|-------|--------|---------------------------------|---------------------------|---------|
10	| 8B    | qwen3  | blk.7.attn_v [4096 x 1024]      | 7,278,168 -> 648,246      | 11.23x  |
11	| 27B   | qwen35 | blk.6.attn_gate [5120 x 6144]   | 54,314,202 -> 4,578,346   | 11.86x  |
12	
13	## Part 1 - what must change to run the 8B model
14	
15	The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same
16	ROI marker at K=51 - two flags and zero rebuilds. Both flags exist because
17	the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM window.
18	
19	- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** (andesim flag). The exact hybrid maximum:
20	  2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects `2G`
21	  outright, so this literal value is required.
22	- **`--no-mmap`** (llama.cpp flag). On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type
23	  accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping AND the
24	  931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. `--no-mmap` drops
25	  the mapping; everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.
26	
27	Guest RAM demand at load, drawn to scale (1 char = 64 MiB):
28	
29	```
30	              0    512  1024 1536 2048 = the 2 GiB window
31	              |----|----|----|----|
32	default (mmap) MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMRRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO   2,582 MiB: FAILS, 534 over
33	with --no-mmap RRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO                    1,483 MiB: fits, 565 free
34	              |----|----|----|----|
35	M = file mapping 1,099   R = repack buffer 931
36	O = other 552 (non-repacked weights 168 + KV cache 72 at -c 512 + compute 312)
37	```
38	
39	```bash
40	cd ~/work/andesim
41	TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
42	  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
43	  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
44	  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
45	  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
46	```
47	
48	## Part 2 - what must change to run the 27B model
49	
50	The 27B (3.8 GB, qwen35) needs three lifts beyond the 8B recipe. Binaries
51	and engine stay the same.
52	
53	1. **Guest RAM beyond 2 GiB.** The andesim runtime now places guest RAM at
54	   the high window 0x8_00000000 (DRAM alias + DRAM_EXT, contiguous) whenever
55	   `--mem-size` exceeds the low window, in both fast and hybrid modes, up to
56	   16G. The vsim leg maps a low-2G alias over the same memory so the RTL
57	   still fetches the low-linked code. At or below 2 GiB the historical map
58	   is kept, so every recorded cycle number stays comparable (re-measured
59	   bit-identical). Commits: andesim `5c134e5`/`1edb88d`/`9d10a6d`,
60	   vsim_andesim `e874381`.
61	2. **`--mem-size 6G --no-mmap`.** With mmap, the 3,891 MiB mapping plus the
62	   ~3.1 GiB repack buffer exceed 6G. `--no-mmap` fits with room to spare.
63	   (An over-budget mmap load does NOT fail fast at this size - it grinds -
64	   so the flag is mandatory at 6G.)
65	3. **The rv64 vec_dot fix** (llama.cpp `17b246b44`). qwen35's delta-net
66	   exercises `ggml_vec_dot_f32`, whose RVV accumulator init used a `_tu`
67	   merge into an uninitialized register; GCC 14 could re-materialize it
68	   under the wrong vector type, corrupting 6 of 8 accumulator registers.
69	   Fixed with a plain init at vlmax. qwen3 (4B/8B) never calls this helper
70	   on its decode path, so their results were always correct and unchanged.
71	   After the fix, 27B rv64 output matches the x86 host byte-for-byte at
72	   temp 0 ("The capital of France is Paris.").
73	
74	```bash
75	cd ~/work/andesim
76	TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
77	  --mem-size 6G --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
78	  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
79	  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf \
80	  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
81	```
82	
83	On qwen35's graph, compiled-in K=51 lands on the layer-6 attention gate
84	(`blk.6.attn_gate.weight [5120 x 6144]`, nrows=2) - self-reported by the
85	`[roi]` line, so the node identity is checked, not assumed.
86	
87	## Part 3 - speedups
88	
89	RTL cycles per model, drawn to scale. The two charts use different scales
90	(8B: 1 char = 150k cycles; 27B: 1 char = 1.1M, about the 7.5x node-size
91	ratio) - the bars look alike because the speedups are alike.
92	
93	```
94	8B, K=51 = attn_v [4096 x 1024]                    (1 char = 150k cycles)
95	pristine   ################################################# 7,278,168   1.00x
96	repack     #######################                           3,475,147   2.09x
97	+prefetch  ###############                                   2,218,540   3.28x
98	+vd4dots   ####                                                648,246  11.23x
99	
100	27B, K=51 = attn_gate [5120 x 6144]                (1 char = 1.1M cycles)
101	pristine   ################################################# 54,314,202  1.00x

# Bonsai 8B and 27B on andesim hybrid: one kernel stack, 11.23x and 11.86x

Engine `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024, ELEN 64, real L3 RTL); 8B measured
2026-08-04, 27B measured 2026-08-05..06. The same Q1_0 optimization chain
(repack -> prefetch -> vd4dots) carries from 4B to 8B to 27B with the
per-element cost almost unchanged:

| model | arch   | K=51 node                       | pristine -> final cycles  | speedup |
|-------|--------|---------------------------------|---------------------------|---------|
| 8B    | qwen3  | blk.7.attn_v [4096 x 1024]      | 7,278,168 -> 648,246      | 11.23x  |
| 27B   | qwen35 | blk.6.attn_gate [5120 x 6144]   | 54,314,202 -> 4,578,346   | 11.86x  |

## Part 1 - what must change to run the 8B model

The 4B recipe carries over unchanged: same four binaries, same engine, same
ROI marker at K=51 - two flags and zero rebuilds. Both flags exist because
the 8B model presses against the 2 GiB guest RAM window.

- **`--mem-size 2097148K`** (andesim flag). The exact hybrid maximum:
  2 GiB minus the 4 KiB hybrid scratch area. Hybrid mode rejects `2G`
  outright, so this literal value is required.
- **`--no-mmap`** (llama.cpp flag). On RISC-V the Q1_0 repack buffer type
  accepts these tensors, so with mmap the 1,099 MiB file mapping AND the
  931 MiB repack buffer are both resident at load time. `--no-mmap` drops
  the mapping; everything else fits with 565 MiB to spare.

Guest RAM demand at load, drawn to scale (1 char = 64 MiB):

```
              0    512  1024 1536 2048 = the 2 GiB window
              |----|----|----|----|
default (mmap) MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMRRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO   2,582 MiB: FAILS, 534 over
with --no-mmap RRRRRRRRRRRRRRROOOOOOOOO                    1,483 MiB: fits, 565 free
              |----|----|----|----|
M = file mapping 1,099   R = repack buffer 931
O = other 552 (non-repacked weights 168 + KV cache 72 at -c 512 + compute 312)
```

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

## Part 2 - what must change to run the 27B model

The 27B (3.8 GB, qwen35) needs three lifts beyond the 8B recipe. Binaries
and engine stay the same.

1. **Guest RAM beyond 2 GiB.** The andesim runtime now places guest RAM at
   the high window 0x8_00000000 (DRAM alias + DRAM_EXT, contiguous) whenever
   `--mem-size` exceeds the low window, in both fast and hybrid modes, up to
   16G. The vsim leg maps a low-2G alias over the same memory so the RTL
   still fetches the low-linked code. At or below 2 GiB the historical map
   is kept, so every recorded cycle number stays comparable (re-measured
   bit-identical). Commits: andesim `5c134e5`/`1edb88d`/`9d10a6d`,
   vsim_andesim `e874381`.
2. **`--mem-size 6G --no-mmap`.** With mmap, the 3,891 MiB mapping plus the
   ~3.1 GiB repack buffer exceed 6G. `--no-mmap` fits with room to spare.
   (An over-budget mmap load does NOT fail fast at this size - it grinds -
   so the flag is mandatory at 6G.)
3. **The rv64 vec_dot fix** (llama.cpp `17b246b44`). qwen35's delta-net
   exercises `ggml_vec_dot_f32`, whose RVV accumulator init used a `_tu`
   merge into an uninitialized register; GCC 14 could re-materialize it
   under the wrong vector type, corrupting 6 of 8 accumulator registers.
   Fixed with a plain init at vlmax. qwen3 (4B/8B) never calls this helper
   on its decode path, so their results were always correct and unchanged.
   After the fix, 27B rv64 output matches the x86 host byte-for-byte at
   temp 0 ("The capital of France is Paris.").

```bash
cd ~/work/andesim
TMPDIR=~/tmp ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 6G --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  ~/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4 -- \
  -m ~/work/llama.cpp/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

On qwen35's graph, compiled-in K=51 lands on the layer-6 attention gate
(`blk.6.attn_gate.weight [5120 x 6144]`, nrows=2) - self-reported by the
`[roi]` line, so the node identity is checked, not assumed.

## Part 3 - speedups

RTL cycles per model, drawn to scale. The two charts use different scales
(8B: 1 char = 150k cycles; 27B: 1 char = 1.1M, about the 7.5x node-size
ratio) - the bars look alike because the speedups are alike.

```
8B, K=51 = attn_v [4096 x 1024]                    (1 char = 150k cycles)
pristine   ################################################# 7,278,168   1.00x
repack     #######################                           3,475,147   2.09x
+prefetch  ###############                                   2,218,540   3.28x
+vd4dots   ####                                                648,246  11.23x

27B, K=51 = attn_gate [5120 x 6144]                (1 char = 1.1M cycles)
pristine   ################################################# 54,314,202  1.00x
repack     #######################                           25,629,722  2.12x
+prefetch  ###############                                   16,317,304  3.33x
+vd4dots   ####                                               4,578,346 11.86x
```

| build          | 8B cycles | 8B total | 27B cycles | 27B total |
|----------------|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| pristine       | 7,278,168 | 1.00x    | 54,314,202 | 1.00x     |
| repack         | 3,475,147 | 2.09x    | 25,629,722 | 2.12x     |
| + prefetch     | 2,218,540 | 3.28x    | 16,317,304 | 3.33x     |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 648,246   | **11.23x** | 4,578,346 | **11.86x** |

The chain transfers because the per-element cost barely moves across an
8.6x range of node sizes. Repack and prefetch are essentially
shape-invariant; vd4dots varies a few percent with the streamed bytes per
row:

| build          | 4B cyc/elem | 8B cyc/elem | 27B cyc/elem |
|----------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|
| pristine       | 1.707       | 1.735       | 1.727        |
| repack         | 0.818       | 0.829       | 0.815        |
| + prefetch     | 0.528       | 0.529       | 0.519        |
| + vd4dots (F9) | 0.138       | 0.155       | 0.146        |

Elements per node: 4B 2560x1024, 8B 4096x1024, 27B 5120x6144; nrows=2 in
all three, so per-activation numbers are these values halved.

<details>
<summary>Appendix - run environment and verification</summary>

- **Models**: Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf 1.16 GB (qwen3, 36 layers, n_embd 4096);
  Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf 3.8 GB (qwen35 hybrid attention, n_embd 5120).
- **Builds**: `bin-pristine` (REPACK=OFF), `bin-baseline` (REPACK=ON, PF=0),
  `bin-prefetch` (PF=1), `bin-d4` (PF=1, Q1_D4=1, includes F9). The vec_dot
  fix is measurement-neutral: fixed-binary 4B K=51 = 362,797 vs 362,799
  recorded (2 cycles, link-layout noise).
- **Success check**: read the output, not the exit code - a good run prints
  the `[roi]` node self-check followed by `[andesim] <N> cycles`.
- **Correctness**: 27B fast-mode run at 6G prints "The capital of France is
  Paris." (temp 0), matching the x86 host reference.
- **Reproducibility**: vsim is deterministic; node counts are repeat-stable.
  Cross-window (>2G vs legacy) comparisons carry a ~0.3% layout-noise bound;
  same-window numbers are exact.
- **Logs**: `~/tmp/8b-runs/{8b,27b}-hybrid-*-k51.log`

</details>

# Optimizing 1-bit LLM Inference for RISC-V Edge Devices

# Author: Pei-Hsiang Hung, Andes Technology

---

## Abstract

1-bit compression has left the lab. You can download the Bonsai 27B model that fits in
3.8 GB and keeps 90% of its FP16 benchmark score. That moves the edge
bottleneck from *does the model fit* to *can the silicon execute it* -- and at
one bit the multiply disappears, since a weight is just a sign. The inner
operation becomes add-or-subtract, which needs wide lanes and cheap instruction
issue rather than a matrix engine. That is vector-CPU territory.

We found upstream llama.cpp using **32 of the 128 byte-lanes** of a 1024-bit
vector unit, plus a serial reduction per 32 columns. Three changes fixed it:
transpose 64 weight rows into the lanes so every lane owns an output row and
the reductions vanish; prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never
reused; and hand the reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, a stock Andes V5 vendor
instruction whose operand shape already matches the repacked tile.

Decode speedup is **12.34x / 11.23x / 11.86x** on Bonsai 4B / 8B / 27B, with
bit-identical output. The first two changes are vendor-neutral and worth
**3.22x** on any compliant RVV core.

Every number is cycle-accurate RTL, taken pre-silicon: a functional model
fast-forwards the 9-minute model load, then hands off to the RTL engine, which
measures one matmul out of 497. Reproducible to the cycle.

---

## Takeaways

1. **For 1-bit models the kernel is a data-layout problem.** Transpose into the
   lanes first; everything else follows from that.
2. **A 4-way int8 dot is worth 3.8x on top of well-written RVV** -- and most of
   the win before it is portable to any RVV core.
3. **Per-kernel pre-silicon measurement changes which optimizations you
   attempt**, because it ranks them correctly when cheaper tools do not.

---


**Speaker:** _to fill in_

**Notes for reviewers:** all cycle figures are measured, not simulated
estimates. Quality-retention figures are the model publisher's, not ours.

# Optimizing 1-bit LLM Inference for RISC-V Edge Devices

# Author: Pei-Hsiang Hung, Andes Technology

---

## Abstract

1-bit compression has left the lab. You can download the Bonsai 27B model that fits in
3.8 GB and keeps 90% of its FP16 benchmark score. That moves the edge
bottleneck from 'Does the model fit?' to 'Can the silicon execute it?'.

At one bit the multiply disappears: a weight is a sign, so the inner operation
is add-or-subtract. The expensive part of an NPU is its multiply array, and
here that array has nothing to do -- you would be paying for multipliers to
compute plus-or-minus one times x. What the work needs instead is many lanes
doing trivial arithmetic, plus the bit manipulation to feed them: sign masks,
bit-planes, per-block scales. A vector CPU already has both, with no extra IP
and no weights to ship across to an accelerator.

We targeted an **Andes AX46MPV**: a single hart with a 1024-bit vector unit,
32 KB of L1 data cache, no L2 and 2 MB of L3 -- wide vectors on a thin memory
system, which is what an edge core actually looks like. On it, upstream
llama.cpp used **32 of the 128 available byte-lanes** per reduction step and
paid a serial reduction every 32 columns.

We optimized the kernel at three levels. Data layout: repack the weights so
every lane owns an output row and the serial reductions disappear. Memory:
prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never reused. ISA: hand
the reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, a stock Andes V5 vendor instruction whose
operand shape already matches the repacked layout.

What we measure is the 1-bit matmul kernel that dominates decode time. On
Bonsai 27B it runs **11.86x** faster than upstream llama.cpp on the same
core, with bit-identical output. The same three changes, applied unchanged,
carry across two more models spanning a 12x range in kernel size and two
different attention architectures:

| model      | arch   | pristine   | repack     | + prefetch | + `vd4dots` | decode speedup |
|------------|--------|------------|------------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| Bonsai 4B  | qwen3  | 4,476,168  | 2,144,213  | 1,389,236  | 362,799     | **12.34x**     |
| Bonsai 8B  | qwen3  | 7,278,168  | 3,475,147  | 2,218,540  | 648,246     | **11.23x**     |
| Bonsai 27B | qwen35 | 54,314,202 | 25,629,722 | 16,317,304 | 4,578,346   | **11.86x**     |

*(cycles, same K=51 projection node in each model, decode / nrows=2)*

Data layout plus prefetch alone -- no vendor-specific instruction -- are worth
**3.2-3.3x** on any compliant RVV core. The 4-way dot adds a further

# Optimizing 1-bit LLM Inference for RISC-V Edge Devices

# Author: Pei-Hsiang Hung, Andes Technology

---

## Abstract

1-bit compression has left the lab. You can download the Bonsai 27B model that fits in
3.8 GB and keeps 90% of its FP16 benchmark score. That moves the edge
bottleneck from 'Does the model fit?' to 'Can the silicon execute it?'.

At one bit the multiply disappears: a weight is a sign, so the inner operation
is add-or-subtract. The expensive part of an NPU is its multiply array, and
here that array has nothing to do -- you would be paying for multipliers to
compute plus-or-minus one times x. What the work needs instead is many lanes
doing trivial arithmetic, plus the bit manipulation to feed them: sign masks,
bit-planes, per-block scales. A vector CPU already has both, with no extra IP
and no weights to ship across to an accelerator.

We targeted an **Andes AX46MPV**: a single hart with a 1024-bit vector unit,
32 KB of L1 data cache, no L2 and 2 MB of L3 -- wide vectors on a thin memory
system, which is what an edge core actually looks like. On it, upstream
llama.cpp used **32 of the 128 available byte-lanes** per reduction step and
paid a serial reduction every 32 columns.

We optimized the kernel at three levels. Data layout: repack the weights so
every lane owns an output row and the serial reductions disappear. Memory:
prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never reused. ISA: hand
the reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, a stock Andes V5 vendor instruction whose
operand shape already matches the repacked layout.

Bonsai 27B it runs **11.86x** faster than upstream llama.cpp on the same
core, with bit-identical output. The same three changes, applied unchanged,
carry across two more models spanning a 12x range in kernel size and two
different attention architectures:

| model      | arch   | pristine   | repack     | + prefetch | + `vd4dots` | decode speedup |
|------------|--------|------------|------------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| Bonsai 4B  | qwen3  | 4,476,168  | 2,144,213  | 1,389,236  | 362,799     | **12.34x**     |

traffic to a quarter, not because of the dot instruction itself.

We measure the cycle with AndeSim's newly developed hybrid mode: a fast
functional model races through the long-running model load, then hands the
machine state to the RTL engine at exactly the matmul we care about --
cycle-accurate, pre-silicon, reproducible to the cycle.

# Optimizing 1-bit LLM Inference for RISC-V Edge Devices

# Author: Pei-Hsiang Hung, Andes Technology

---

## Abstract

1-bit compression has left the lab. You can download the Bonsai 27B model that fits in
3.8 GB and keeps 90% of its FP16 benchmark score. That moves the edge
bottleneck from 'Does the model fit?' to 'Can the silicon execute it?'.

At one bit the multiply disappears: a weight is a sign, so the inner operation
is add-or-subtract. The expensive part of an NPU is its multiply array, and
here that array has nothing to do -- you would be paying for multipliers to
compute plus-or-minus one times x. What the work needs instead is many lanes
doing trivial arithmetic, plus the bit manipulation to feed them: sign masks,
bit-planes, per-block scales. A vector CPU already has both, with no extra IP
and no weights to ship across to an accelerator.

We targeted an **Andes AX46MPV**: a single hart with a 1024-bit vector unit,
32 KB of L1 data cache, no L2 and 2 MB of L3 -- wide vectors on a thin memory
system, which is what an edge core actually looks like. On it, upstream
llama.cpp used **32 of the 128 available byte-lanes** per reduction step and
paid a serial reduction every 32 columns.

We optimized the kernel at three levels. Data layout: repack the weights so
every lane owns an output row and the serial reductions disappear. Memory:
prefetch the weight stream, which is read once and never reused. ISA: hand
the reduction to `nds.vd4dots.vv`, a stock Andes V5 vendor instruction whose
operand shape already matches the repacked layout.

What we measure is the 1-bit matmul kernel that dominates decode time. On
Bonsai 27B it runs **11.86x** faster than upstream llama.cpp on the same
core, with bit-identical output. The same three changes, applied unchanged,
carry across two more models spanning a 12x range in kernel size and two
different attention architectures:

| model      | arch   | pristine   | repack     | + prefetch | + `vd4dots` | decode speedup |
|------------|--------|------------|------------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| Bonsai 4B  | qwen3  | 4,476,168  | 2,144,213  | 1,389,236  | 362,799     | **12.34x**     |
| Bonsai 8B  | qwen3  | 7,278,168  | 3,475,147  | 2,218,540  | 648,246     | **11.23x**     |
| Bonsai 27B | qwen35 | 54,314,202 | 25,629,722 | 16,317,304 | 4,578,346   | **11.86x**     |

*(cycles, same K=51 projection node in each model, decode / nrows=2)*

Data layout plus prefetch alone -- no vendor-specific instruction -- are worth
**3.2-3.3x** on any compliant RVV core. The 4-way dot adds a further
**3.4-3.8x** on top of that: reading 4 columns per lane moves the same bytes
in a quarter as many load instructions, which is what moves the needle when
the kernel is issue-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.

We measure the cycle with AndeSim's newly developed hybrid mode: a fast
functional model races through the long-running model load, then hands the
machine state to the RTL engine at exactly the matmul we care about --
cycle-accurate, pre-silicon, reproducible to the cycle.

---

## Takeaways

1. **For 1-bit models the kernel is a data-layout problem.** Transpose into
   the lanes first; everything else follows from that.
2. **Most of the win is vendor-neutral.** Repack + prefetch alone reach
   3.2-3.3x on any compliant RVV core; the vendor 4-way dot is the last
   3.4-3.8x, not the bulk of it.
3. **The chain transfers across models, not just within one.** Same three
   changes, same order, unchanged code, 11.2x-12.3x decode speedup across two
   architectures and a 12x range in kernel size.
4. **Per-kernel pre-silicon measurement changes which optimizations you
   attempt**, because it ranks them correctly when cheaper tools do not.

---


**Speaker:** _to fill in_

**Notes for reviewers:** all cycle figures are measured, not simulated
estimates. Quality-retention figures are the model publisher's, not ours.

## Reference
https://makerpro.cc/how-can-bonsai-27b-disrupt-the-boundaries-between-local-llm-and-slm/

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a riscv64 llama.cpp binary under Andes QEMU (user-mode).
#
# Usage:   ./run-rv64-qemu.sh <binary-name-or-path> [args...]
# Example: ./run-rv64-qemu.sh llama-bench -m model.gguf -p 8 -n 4 -r 1 -t 1
#
# Overridable via environment:
#   ANDES_ROOT  Andes SW release root
#   QEMU        Andes linux-user qemu-riscv64
#   SYSROOT     toolchain glibc sysroot (matches the xandes-built libc)
#   BIN_DIR     directory with the cross-built binaries and libggml*/libllama* .so
#   QEMU_CPU    QEMU cpu string; zfh/zvfh must be enabled explicitly:
#               andes-ax45mpv does not enable them by default and
#               ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16 (vfncvt.f.f.w) SIGILLs without zvfh
#   MODEL       default model, added as "-m $MODEL" when no -m is given
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ANDES_ROOT=${ANDES_ROOT:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542}
QEMU=${QEMU:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-qemu/linux/qemu-riscv64}
SYSROOT=${SYSROOT:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d/sysroot}
BIN_DIR=${BIN_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/build-rv64/bin}
QEMU_CPU=${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512,zfh=true,zvfh=true}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <binary-name-or-path> [args...]" >&2
    exit 1
fi

BIN=$1
shift
[ -f "$BIN" ] || BIN=$BIN_DIR/$BIN

MODEL=${MODEL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf}
case "$(basename "$BIN")" in
    llama-cli|llama-completion|llama-bench|llama-server|llama-perplexity)
        has_model=false
        for arg in "$@"; do
            [ "$arg" = "-m" ] && has_model=true
        done
        if ! $has_model; then
            set -- "$@" -m "$MODEL"
        fi
        ;;
esac

exec "$QEMU" \
    -L "$SYSROOT" \
    -E LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$BIN_DIR" \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    "$BIN" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Codegen gate for the Q1_D4 kernels (ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp).
#
# Two things this catches that no result test can:
#
#  1. A path silently falls back. Q1_D4 changes the sign-plane order AND the
#     kernel; if gemv or gemm never got a vd4dots kernel it still returns
#     correct numbers through the generic C path, just ~3x slower. Counting
#     nds.vd4dots is the only way to see which one is really on the
#     instruction. (This was real: gemm ran generic for the whole F8 sweep.)
#
#  2. The F5 weight prefetch is dead-code eliminated. Same trap as
#     check-prefetch.sh guards, but that script counts per ENTRY point and the
#     d4 kernels stay out of line, so it reads 0 there and cannot be used on a
#     d4 build. Counted here instead, in the kernel body.
#
#  3. vtype churn (F9) creeps back. The kernels alternate between the byte
#     view (vlm, vmerge) and the 32-bit view (vmv.v.x, the dot), and every
#     alternation costs a vsetvli that does no arithmetic - 4 per dot in the
#     original gemv, 40% of its inner loop. The fix (batch by element width,
#     several dots per asm block) is invisible to every result test. Measured
#     as vsetvli between the FIRST and LAST dot, per dot gap, so the prologue
#     and the fp16-scale expansion do not pollute it. Budget: at most 1.
#
#  4. The activation broadcast collapses into vlse32.v vd,(rs1),zero. A
#     stride-0 strided load is element-serial on this core - 18x slower than
#     lw + vmv.v.x - and GCC contracts "load a word, splat it" into exactly
#     that whenever the value is not pinned in a GPR first (q1_bcast_act4).
#     Results are identical, so only the assembly shows it.
#
# The kernels are file-static, so each is checked in its own body; if the
# compiler inlined it away the entry point is checked instead. A kernel with
# no label and no inlined copy has been dead-code eliminated, which is exactly
# the "fell back to generic" failure.
#
# Reuses an existing CMake build's compile line for that one TU, so -march,
# -O level and includes are never duplicated here.
#
# Usage: ./check-vd4dots.sh [build-dir]      env: BUILD, OLEVELS
set -e
LLAMA=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
BUILD=${1:-${BUILD:-b-d4}}
OLEVELS=${OLEVELS:-"O2 O3 Os"}
SRC=$LLAMA/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp
# "<kernel static fn> <entry point it inlines into>"
KERNELS="q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024:ggml_gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0 q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024:ggml_gemm_q1_0_64x1_q8_0"

CC_DB=$LLAMA/$BUILD/compile_commands.json
[ -f "$CC_DB" ] || { echo "no $CC_DB (build it with bash build.sh d4)"; exit 1; }

ENTRY=$(python3 - "$CC_DB" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
for d in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
    if d['file'].endswith('arch/riscv/repack.cpp'):

# Reproducing the Q1_0 RISC-V kernel optimizations

Four checks, cheapest first. Each one proves a different claim from the
summit abstract; run them in order and stop wherever you have enough
confidence.

| level | proves                                   | needs                | time     |
|-------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| 1     | repack layout is numerically correct       | toolchain + qemu-user | ~1 min   |
| 2     | prefetch / `vd4dots` are actually emitted  | an existing build dir | ~1 min   |
| 3     | whole-model output is bit-identical        | andesim, fast mode    | ~5 min   |
| 4     | the cycle counts in the abstract           | andesim, hybrid + RTL | minutes/binary |

## Prerequisites

```bash
export LLAMA=~/work/llama.cpp
export ANDESIM=~/work/andesim
export TC=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d
cd "$LLAMA"

# confirm the pieces exist before running anything below
test -x "$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" && echo "toolchain: OK"
test -x "$ANDESIM/andesim"          && echo "andesim: OK"
test -f models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf  && echo "4B model: OK"
```

## Level 1 - repack layout correctness (qemu-user)

This checks the math, independent of the vendor instruction: pack random
weights, run the packed gemv/gemm, compare against a reference. Run it once
with the plain-RVV layout and once with the `vd4dots` layout - both must
pass, since they share the test and differ only in `D4`.

```bash
D4=0 bash build-d4-qemu.sh   # plain RVV layout (control)
D4=1 bash build-d4-qemu.sh   # vd4dots layout

QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024,zfh=true,zvfh=true \
  BIN_DIR=build-d4-qemu/bin ./run-rv64-qemu.sh test-repack-q1_0
```

Expect `13/13 repack cases passed` both times. `D4=1`'s build directory is
overwritten by the second `build-d4-qemu.sh` call, so run the test between
the two builds if you want to see both pass lines separately.

These binaries are dynamic and built with a plain `-march` specifically so
qemu-user can run them directly. The `build.sh` binaries below (`bin-*`) are
static with the Zc compressed-instruction extensions, built for andesim -
qemu-user is not the right runner for those; use `run-rv64-qemu.sh` only on
`build-d4-qemu.sh` output.

## Level 2 - confirm the instructions are actually emitted

Correct output doesn't prove the fast path ran - a silently-generic fallback
gives the same numbers, just slower. These gates disassemble the built
object and count instructions.

```bash
bash build.sh prefetch d4     # needs the two builds these gates check

BUILD=b-prefetch ./check-prefetch.sh   # expects 2x prefetch.r per entry point
BUILD=b-d4        ./check-vd4dots.sh   # expects nds.vd4dots in gemv AND gemm,
                                        # no vtype churn, no strided broadcast
```

Both print `PASS: ...`. Either failing means the codegen regressed even
though Level 1's numbers still look right - that's the failure mode these
exist to catch.

## Level 3 - whole-model output, bit-identical (andesim fast mode)

No RTL yet - a functional model runs the real Bonsai-4B model end to end and
compares generated text between the prefetch build and the no-prefetch
baseline.

```bash
bash build.sh pristine baseline prefetch d4   # if not already built
bash verify.sh
```

Expect:
```
PREFETCH: <generated continuation>
BASELINE: <same continuation>
PASS: prefetch output is bit-identical to baseline
```

## Level 4 - the cycle counts behind the speedup numbers

This is the slow one: andesim hybrid mode fast-forwards the model load with
a functional model, then hands off to the RTL engine at the K=51 attention
node and counts real cycles.

```bash
bash measure.sh pristine baseline prefetch d4
```

Expect, on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (cycles will vary by a fraction of a
percent run to run; the ratios are what matters):

| build    | cycles    | vs. pristine |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| pristine | 4,476,168 | 1.00x        |
| baseline | 2,144,213 | 2.09x        |
| prefetch | 1,389,236 | 3.22x        |
| d4       |   362,799 | 12.34x       |

<details>
<summary>Appendix - 8B/27B, script reference, troubleshooting</summary>

### Reproducing the 8B and 27B numbers

Same four binaries, same `measure.sh`-style invocation, different
`--mem-size`/`--no-mmap` flags because the bigger models press against the
guest RAM window. Full commands and the per-model reasoning are in
`q1_0_8b_hybrid.md`.

```bash
# 8B
cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 2097148K --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  "$LLAMA/bin-d4" -- -m "$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf" \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1

# 27B
cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
  --mem-size 6G --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  "$LLAMA/bin-d4" -- -m "$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf" \
  --no-mmap -no-cnv --prompt 'The capital of France is' -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

### Script reference

| script              | what it does                                            |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `build.sh`          | builds `bin-pristine/baseline/prefetch/d4[-nopf]` for andesim |
| `build-d4-qemu.sh`  | builds a dynamic `test-repack-q1_0` for qemu-user (Level 1) |
| `check-prefetch.sh` | codegen gate: counts `prefetch.r` per entry point         |
| `check-vd4dots.sh`  | codegen gate: counts `nds.vd4dots`, checks for vtype churn and strided loads |
| `verify.sh`         | fast-mode bit-exact check, prefetch vs. baseline           |
| `measure.sh`        | hybrid-mode cycle counts, any subset of the four builds    |
| `run-rv64-qemu.sh`  | runs a riscv64 binary under qemu-user                      |

### Troubleshooting

- **`run-rv64-qemu.sh` exits 139 (SIGSEGV), no output at all**: you pointed it
  at a `build.sh` binary (`bin-pristine`, `b-d4/bin/...`, etc). Those are
  static Zc-extension binaries for andesim; qemu-user only runs the plain
  `-march` binaries from `build-d4-qemu.sh`.
- **`check-*.sh` says "no compile_commands.json"**: that build dir was
  configured without `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`. `build.sh` already
  sets this; if you hand-rolled a `cmake` call, add the flag and reconfigure.
- **andesim run looks stuck**: hybrid mode's RTL leg runs at a few kHz: budget
  minutes per binary, not seconds. Watch for the `[roi]` line first (model
  load finished, ROI entered) - if that never appears, the model load itself
  is the problem, not the measurement.

</details>
